content: The interaction between aluminum hydroxide or magnesium hydroxide and various medications primarily involves changes in gastrointestinal (GI) absorption or gastric pH, which can either increase or decrease the levels and effects of the co-administered drugs. 1. Fleroxacin: Magnesium hydroxide reduces the absorption of fleroxacin in the GI tract, leading to decreased drug levels. This interaction is not related to changes in gastric pH. Separate administration of the two agents by at least 2 hours. This applies only to oral formulations of both drugs. Monitor therapy closely. 2. Elvitegravir/Cobicistat/Emtricitabine/Tenofovir DF: Aluminum hydroxide decreases the absorption of this combination product in the GI tract, resulting in reduced drug levels. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 3. Enalapril: Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of enalapril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 4. Ephedrine: Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels or effects of ephedrine by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor therapy. 5. Erythromycin (Base, Ethylsuccinate, Lactobionate, Stearate): Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels of various erythromycin formulations through an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 6. Esmolol: Aluminum hydroxide decreases esmolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 7. Ethambutol: Aluminum hydroxide increases ethambutol levels due to cation binding in the GI tract. Avoid administering aluminum hydroxide-containing antacids for at least 4 hours after ethambutol dosing. Use caution and monitor therapy. 8. Etidronate: Aluminum hydroxide decreases etidronate levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 9. Ferric Maltol, Ferrous Fumarate, Ferrous Gluconate, Ferrous Sulfate: Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of these iron supplements by increasing gastric pH. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 10. Flecainide: Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels or effects of flecainide by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor therapy. 11. Fosamprenavir: Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of fosamprenavir by increasing gastric pH. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 12. Fosinopril: Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of fosinopril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 13. Gabapentin, Gabapentin Enacarbil: Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels of gabapentin and its prodrug by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 14. Gefitinib: Aluminum hydroxide decreases gefitinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Separate administration by at least 6 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 15. Gemifloxacin: Magnesium hydroxide decreases gemifloxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 16. Glipizide, Glyburide: Aluminum hydroxide increases the levels or effects of these antidiabetic agents by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor therapy. 17. Ibandronate: Aluminum hydroxide decreases ibandronate levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 18. Imidapril: Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of imidapril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 19. Iron Dextran Complex, Iron Sucrose: Aluminum hydroxide decreases the levels or effects of these iron formulations by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor therapy. 20. Isoniazid: Aluminum hydroxide decreases isoniazid levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 21. Itraconazole: Aluminum hydroxide decreases itraconazole levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Administer acid-neutralizing medicines at least 2 hours before or after itraconazole. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 22. Ketoconazole: Aluminum hydroxide decreases ketoconazole levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 23. Labetalol: Aluminum hydroxide decreases labetalol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 24. Lactulose: Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of lactulose through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 25. Lanthanum Carbonate: Aluminum hydroxide interacts with lanthanum carbonate through cation binding in the GI tract. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or after lanthanum. Use caution and monitor therapy. 26. Ledipasvir/Sofosbuvir: Aluminum hydroxide decreases ledipasvir levels due to reduced solubility at higher pH levels. Separate administration by 4 hours. Use caution and monitor therapy. 27. Levofloxacin: Magnesium hydroxide decreases levofloxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 28. Levoketoconazole: Aluminum hydroxide decreases levoketoconazole levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 29. Lisdexamfetamine: Aluminum hydroxide increases lisdexamfetamine levels or effects by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor therapy. 30. Lisinopril: Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of lisinopril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 31. Memantine: Aluminum hydroxide increases memantine levels or effects by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor therapy. 32. Methscopolamine: Aluminum hydroxide decreases methscopolamine levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 33. Methylphenidate: Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of methylphenidate by altering its GI absorption. For extended-release formulations, consider separating administration of antacids and methylphenidate. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 34. Metoprolol: Aluminum hydroxide decreases metoprolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 35. Mexiletine: Aluminum hydroxide increases mexiletine levels or effects by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor therapy. 36. Moexipril: Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of moexipril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 37. Moxifloxacin: Magnesium hydroxide decreases moxifloxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 38. Mycophenolate: Aluminum hydroxide decreases mycophenolate levels by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor therapy. 39. Nadolol: Aluminum hydroxide decreases nadolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 40. Nebivolol: Aluminum hydroxide decreases nebivolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 41. Neratinib: Aluminum hydroxide decreases neratinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Separate administration by 3 hours. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 42. Nilotinib: Aluminum hydroxide decreases nilotinib levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer antacids 2 hours before or after nilotinib. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 43. Nitrofurantoin: Aluminum hydroxide decreases nitrofurantoin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 44. Ofloxacin: Magnesium hydroxide decreases ofloxacin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 45. Omadacycline: Aluminum hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide decrease omadacycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration of tetracyclines from multivalent cation-containing products. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 46. Pamidronate: Aluminum hydroxide decreases pamidronate levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 47. Pancrelipase: Magnesium hydroxide reduces the effects of pancrelipase through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 48. Penbutolol: Aluminum hydroxide decreases penbutolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 49. Penicillamine: Aluminum hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide decrease penicillamine levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 50. Perindopril: Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of perindopril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 51. Pexidartinib: Aluminum hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide decrease pexidartinib levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 52. Pindolol: Aluminum hydroxide decreases pindolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 53. Polysaccharide Iron: Aluminum hydroxide decreases polysaccharide iron levels by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor therapy. 54. Posaconazole: Aluminum hydroxide decreases posaconazole levels by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor therapy. 55. Propranolol: Aluminum hydroxide decreases propranolol levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 56. Pseudoephedrine: Aluminum hydroxide increases pseudoephedrine levels or effects by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor therapy. 57. Quinapril: Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of quinapril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 58. Quinidine: Aluminum hydroxide increases quinidine levels or effects by enhancing passive renal tubular reabsorption in a basic urine environment. Use caution and monitor therapy. 59. Ramipril: Aluminum hydroxide reduces the effects of ramipril through an unspecified interaction mechanism. Use caution and monitor therapy. 60. Rifampin: Aluminum hydroxide decreases rifampin levels by reducing its absorption. Administer rifampin at least 1 hour before antacids. Use caution and monitor therapy. 61. Rilpivirine: Aluminum hydroxide decreases rilpivirine levels by increasing gastric pH. Administer antacids at least 2 hours before or 4 hours after rilpivirine. For combination products like dolutegravir/rilpivirine, administer antacids at least 4 hours before or 6 hours after. Modify therapy and monitor closely. 62. Riociguat: Aluminum hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide decrease riociguat levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by at least 1 hour. Use caution and monitor therapy. 63. Risedronate: Aluminum hydroxide decreases risedronate levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 64. Rose Hips: Aluminum hydroxide decreases rose hips levels by increasing gastric pH. Use caution and monitor therapy. 65. Rosuvastatin: Aluminum hydroxide decreases rosuvastatin levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration by 2 hours. This applies only to oral forms of both agents. Use caution and monitor therapy. 66. Sarecycline: Aluminum hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide decrease sarecycline levels by inhibiting GI absorption. Separate administration of tetracyclines from multivalent cation-containing products. Modify therapy and monitor closely. This list provides detailed guidance on the interactions between antacids and various medications, emphasizing the need for careful monitoring, therapy adjustments, and appropriate timing of administration to minimize adverse effects.
